speaker: Arne Slot
quote_text:
The first Trent question. Can I? Sorry, but what  did you what did you mean for Trent then? If  
you I'd rather ask you about the gang, but as you  said about Trent, what did you feel what did you  
like about? I said to everyone that asked me that  question, that it is a privilege to live in Europe  
where everybody can have his own opinion and  everybody can express his own opinion. And that  
is something that we saw today as well. So a few  of them were not happy with him. I think all of  
them were not happy with him leaving the club, but  a few of them showed it in a way that they booed  
him and a few of them clapped. And the only thing  I can say about it is that I owe it to the players  
and to the club and to the staff for everyone that  worked so hard for us to win a game of football.  
To try to do that, and if we are after 70  minutes to two, Conor can't continue when I  
have a world-class fullback on the bench. I bring  him in and I think it's a big compliment for him  
because you can understand how mixed the emotions  were in his head probably as well. That you bring  
in a performance like that tells you why I think,  why everybody thinks he's a world-class fullback  
because with him we were quite close to winning  this game and that's what I owe. to the players  
in the dressing room that work so hard every  single day to make decisions to try to win the  
game. Do you feel sorry for him on a personal  level? Because you've clearly worked with him  
for so many months. He's been outstanding for you  for this club. You know, it must be difficult for  
Trent right now. It's definitely difficult  for him because I think he said himself how  
difficult it was to leave this football club.  And that is something that is important for us  
to hear as well, because we have to make it as  difficult as possible. And fortunately for us,  
many stay like Virgil and Mo. Trent made the  decision to go. But yeah, it is the way you want  
to look at it. I don't know. I haven't asked  him. But maybe he's positively surprised how  
the reactions were today. I don't know because I  haven't spoken to him. But it was clear that they  
were mixed reactions. So it wasn't all negative.  And as it went onwards, the moment he had to take  
a free kick, everybody was cheering for him for  him to score. And he was close. So, I'm not even  
sure if he if what he if he has negative feelings  about today, maybe, maybe, but again, I haven't  
spoken to him. It's it's it's it's not even that  negative as you supposedly think it is. Anna,  
do you not feel though that there was a bit of  a distraction to the performance though when he  
entered the pitch? and maybe play, or the rest of  the team were distracted by what was going on? No,  
that's what I'm glad you asked this question,  because that was the positive thing about it.  
I think the moment he ended the pitch, I think  3 or 4 minutes later, also after we've made the  
substitution to bring an extra attacker in to try  to, even though we were not in the best part of  
our game, but we did brought Diogo Jota in to  play up front together with Darwin Núñez. And  
from that moment on, we took the game, because  immediately it was the yellow card as a result  
of the red card. So I didn't feel any distraction.  That was something I have to give him credit for,  
but also the team. I think in the last 15 to  20 minutes were the best 15 to 20 minutes of  
the second-half. But that wasn't that difficult  after the first 20. But you said it was a few, it  
was more than a few. The losers had been touched  when he came up. That must be very hard for him  
to take. Yeah, but there were also more than a few  that clapped for him. So the word for you, yeah,  
you can maybe, I don't know, I don't, I couldn't  count them, but was it half-half? Was it 60-40? I  
have no clue. Yeah, 60 in positive and 40 negative  or the opposite? More negative. Okay. Yeah, but I  
think if you clap, it's not as loud as if you boo.  But I didn't count the amount of people that were  
booing and the ones that clapped for him. But  like I said, they have the right to express  
their opinion. I think the first thing they did  is give credit to Steven Gerrard one more time  
for the player he's been for this club. Then  they sung for Conor Bradley, who deserved that  
completely because he played great, 60, 70 minutes  long. Although he had to block the cross with the  
2-1, but that I will tell him this week. But he  played really well. And then afterwards, yeah,  
if you tell me it was 60-40-50-50-40, I don't  know. But what I do know is clapping is not as  
loud as booing. Can I just ask you about the next  time you're here with the trophy presentation, do  
you have to give serious consideration to whether  Trent's involved in that game? Because, you know,  
booing in any shape or form will take the edge off  that water. I don't think there's any possibility,  
whatever can happen, that can take the edge of us  winning this league, the 20th league title. I was  
here 2 weeks ago and there's nothing, yeah, maybe  there can happen. happened a few things, but those  
things will be much worse than what we are talking  about that can take the edge of us winning the  
league title. But then we have to think of things  that I don't want to think about. You wouldn't  
consider leaving him out for the whole game, not  in the match. The thing I consider is I want to  
win a game of football. And if I think we think  we can win this one with Trent, I owe it to his  
teammates, to the fans, because they hired me to  win as much games of football as possible. And if  
I think there's a better chance of winning it with  Trent, I will. If I think, which I don't think,  
it's a distraction or whatever can happen for us  not to play a good game of football, then I might,  
might, might make another decision. But I think  Trent showed today why I brought him in, because  
he was very close with a few fantastic crosses  for us to win the game. And aside from Trent,  
what did you make of the performers in the game  today? Unfortunately, we had 15 to 20 minutes  
where we played with the same intensity and it's  not completely bad, but I miss a little bit and  
that were the first 15 to 20 minutes in the  second-half, which were similar to what we saw  
last week where we played really good with the  ball, came in so many promising positions, but  
in the final third we weren't that decisive and  defending last week was the few goals we conceded  
was, no, that's put it positive, not so good. And  that I saw in the 1st 15 minutes after halftime.  
But the first half was great. And I think all  over, this is why people like the Premier League  
so much. Two great teams that are competing with  each other in a fantastic game of football. Both  
teams showing so much quality. And four goals,  2-2, both teams could have won it in the end.  
This is what makes the Premier League so special.  And this is also what we have to try as managers,  
not only to win games, but also make sure the  fans like what they see. Thank you. Thank you.
title: Arne Slot post-match press conference | Liverpool 2-2 Arsenal
